pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:53 still evaluates every rule against an UNSCOPED 1-day bundle (and useObservabilityData.ts:70 against the tab's range/persona) under the one rule.id cooldown the scoped Rust evaluator also reads, so a wrong-scope client fire mutes the correct server alert for an hour

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:53 fetches getOverviewBundle with no persona scope, yet the fire it produces consumes the rule.id cooldown that src-tauri/src/commands/execution/alert_evaluator.rs:216 honours for the persona-scoped evaluation - the key is right, the condition written under it is the wrong scope's
src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useGlobalAlertEvaluator.ts:67 evaluation runs on a setInterval tick, not inside an admission decision - there is no request path to tax
src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:463 the only scope a rule carries is persona_id, an agent (infrastructure axis), never a key or customer

pairs.registryProposal: Re-judged a same-day verdict at the unchanged digest: the deviation is real, but it fits scoped-dedup-keys awkwardly - rule.id IS a fully specific key and sharing it across two evaluators is what the technique prescribes (the key names the condition, not the detector). The failure is a second evaluator computing the condition at the wrong scope under that shared key. The technique could name this: 'every producer writing under a shared key must evaluate the same scope, or the least-scoped producer owns the cooldown'.

src/stores/slices/overview/alertSlice.ts:387 delivery is a fire-and-forget api.createFiredAlert promise from a timer-driven evaluation; no admission path exists to protect

pairs.registryProposal: Coverage hole in the consumer's context map: src-tauri/src/commands/execution/alert_evaluator.rs (the server-side breach evaluator this subject governs most directly) belongs to NO context in context-map.json, so no pair can ever judge it. Its payload (:262-271) also carries no attribution. | src-tauri/src/engine/webhook_notifier.rs is filed under context 'output-stream-parser', which this subject is not paired with; dispatch_to_url (:414-427) sends alert_fired payloads to operator-supplied URLs through SSRF_SAFE_HTTP (vetting realized) but UNSIGNED (notification-channel-security deviation nobody can record until that file is mapped to an alerting/notifications context).
